theory.intro: A **scale drawing** — a map, plan or blueprint — is a similar figure of a real object. Its scale is written as the ratio **image : original**, usually in the form $1:n$.
facts: A scale of $1:n$ means $1$ unit on the drawing represents $n$ units in real life.
$\text{real length}=\text{drawing length}\times n$, and $\text{drawing length}=\text{real length}\div n$.
Convert both lengths to the same unit before comparing, then give the answer in a sensible unit.
To find the scale from a matched pair, write $\text{drawing}:\text{real}$ in the same unit and simplify to $1:n$.
A scale of $n:1$ is a magnification — the drawing is larger than the real object, as for cells and insects.
steps: Write the scale as a ratio, image : original.
Decide whether the known length is on the drawing (image) or in real life (original).
Multiply or divide by the scale number, then convert to an appropriate unit.

workedExamples.question_text: On a plan, $3$ cm represents $12$ m in real life. Write the scale as a ratio in simplest form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert both lengths to centimetres, then simplify image : original.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3\text{ cm}:12\text{ m}\\&=3\text{ cm}:1200\text{ cm}\\&=1:400\end{aligned}$

The ratio image : original is $1:250$, so multiply the plan length by $250$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Real length}&=8\times250\text{ cm}\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A map uses a scale of $1:20\,000$. A trail is $1.8$ km long in real life. Find its length on the map in centimetres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$1.8\text{ km}=180\,000\text{ cm}$.
The ratio image : original is $1:20\,000$, so divide the real length by $20\,000$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Map length}&=180\,000\div20\,000\text{ cm}\\&=9\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A length of $6$ cm on a blueprint represents $240$ m in real life. Find the scale in the form $1:n$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$240\text{ m}=24\,000\text{ cm}$.
Write image : original and divide both numbers by $6$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6:24\,000\\&=1:4000\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A scientist uses a scale of $200:1$ to draw a cell.
(a) A drawing is $6$ cm long. Find the real cell length in millimetres.
(b) Another cell is $0.04$ mm long. Find its drawing length in millimetres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Image : original is $200:1$, so divide the drawing length by $200$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Real length}&=6\div200\text{ cm}\\&=0.03\text{ cm}\\&=0.3\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$
(b) Multiply the real length by $200$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Drawing length}&=0.04\times200\text{ mm}\\&=8\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$

$12\text{ m}=1200\text{ cm}$.
Use the known pair to find image : original.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3:1200\\&=1:400\end{aligned}$
Apply this scale to the other wall.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Real length}&=5\times400\text{ cm}\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular room on a plan of scale $1:200$ measures $3.5$ cm by $2$ cm. Find its real area in square metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Find both real dimensions before calculating the area.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Real length}&=3.5\times200\text{ cm}\\&=700\text{ cm}\\&=7\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Real width}&=2\times200\text{ cm}\\&=400\text{ cm}\\&=4\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=7\times4\\&=28\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A drawing shows an insect at $30$ times its real length. A student writes the scale as $1:30$. Explain the error and write the correct scale.
workedExamples.solution_text: Scale is written as image : original. The image is $30$ times the original length, so the correct scale is $30:1$. The ratio $1:30$ describes a reduction.

foundation.question_text:
A scale drawing is made so that $1$ cm on the drawing represents $2$ m in real life.
Write this scale as a ratio in simplest form.

On a plan, $5$ mm represents $20$ m in real life.
Write this scale as a ratio in simplest form.

A map has a scale of $1:500$.
A road is $24$ mm long on the map.
Find the real length of the road, in metres.

A plan has a scale of $1:200$.
A path measures $7$ cm on the plan.
Find the real length of the path, in metres.

A map has a scale of $1:5000$.
Two landmarks are $250$ m apart in real life.
Find the distance between them on the map, in centimetres.

You draw a scale diagram of a tree using a scale of $1:150$.
The tree is $45$ m high.
How high should the tree be in your drawing, in centimetres?

A length of $4$ cm on a scale drawing represents $20$ m in real life.
Find the scale of the drawing, in the form $1:n$.

A scientist draws a cell using a scale of $100:1$.
The drawing of the cell is $8$ cm long.
Find the real length of the cell, in millimetres.

development.question_text:
A map has a scale of $1:50\,000$.
Two towns are $17$ cm apart on the map.
Find the real distance between them, in kilometres.

A map has a scale of $1:25\,000$.
A walking trail is $3.4$ cm long on the map.
Find the real length of the trail, in metres.

A map has a scale of $1:100\,000$.
Two towns are $66$ km apart in real life.
Find the distance between them on the map, in centimetres.

A length of $32$ cm on a blueprint represents $1600$ m in real life.
Find the scale of the blueprint, in the form $1:n$.

A real-life distance of $1.5$ km is represented by $60$ cm on a plan.
Find the scale of the plan, in the form $1:n$.

A scientist draws a bacterium using a scale of $500:1$.
The real bacterium is $0.01$ mm long.
How long should the bacterium be in the drawing, in millimetres?

mastery.solution_text:
$4\text{ cm}:8\text{ m}$
$=4\text{ cm}:800\text{ cm}$
$=1:200$
$\text{real}=6\times200$
$=1200\text{ cm}$
$=12\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular room on a house plan of scale $1:100$ measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm.
Find the real area of the room, in square metres.

A student magnifies a drawing of an ant so that the drawing is larger than the real ant, and writes the scale as $1:50$.
Explain what is wrong, and give the scale written correctly.
mastery.solution_text: A magnified drawing is larger than the real object, so the image length is greater than the original length. Written as image : original the larger number must come first, so the scale should be $50:1$, not $1:50$.
